articles.headline: Luka Doncic's 53-point explosion pushes scoring average past 40 as Lakers roll
articles.description: Luka Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points in Friday's 124-118 win over the Blazers, raising his scoring average to 40.1.
articles.headlineJa: ルカ・ドンチッチが53得点の猛攻で平均得点40点超え、レイカーズは快進撃を続ける
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜日のブレイザーズ戦で124-118と勝利した試合で、ルカ・ドンチッチがシーズンハイの53得点を記録し、平均得点を40.1点にまで引き上げた。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Though Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and James Harden came somewhat close, no NBA player has averaged at least 40 points in a season since Wilt Chamberlain in 1962-63.

Believe it or not, Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic is on pace through his first nine games of the season to reach that historic benchmark thanks to his latest 50-point explosion.

Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points to lead the Lakers to a 124-118 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. The Slovenian star is averaging a career-high 40.1 points and is captaining the NBA's No. 1 offense.

"Luka can do some things that maybe a handful, if not no one, can do in basketball," Lakers coach JJ Redick said.

Chamberlain is the only player to score more than Doncic's 361 points through his first nine games in a season. The Hall of Fame center had 472 points through nine games in 1962-63 and 455 points in the 1961-62 season, according to ESPN Research.

Chamberlain went on to average an NBA record 50.4 points in 1961-62 and 44.8 points in 1962-63. Jordan's 37.1 points per game in 1986-87 is the NBA's highest mark during the 3-point era. Harden's 36.1 points per game in 2018-19 was the most prolific scoring season of the 21st century. And Bryant's 35.4 points were the most by a Lakers player since the NBA/ABA merger in 1976.

Can Doncic, whose career high for a season is 33.9 points per game with the 2023-24 Dallas Mavericks, join Chamberlain in averaging at least 40 points?

"It's obviously a long season," Doncic said. "We're 10 games in. We've got 72 left. As long as we're winning, I'm good. I got [the shots] up today, I'm not going to lie. Hopefully, it continues, but you never know."

Doncic, 27, is taking full advantage of his new role as the undisputed face of the Lakers after LeBron James' offseason departure to the Philadelphia 76ers. Entering Friday, Doncic was leading the league in scoring, shot attempts, 3-point attempts, free throw attempts, usage rate, player efficiency rating and win shares.

Against the Blazers, Doncic exceeded 40 points for the sixth time this season and topped 50 for the second time. He ranks tied for 10th all time with 11 career games of scoring at least 50 points and is fifth among active players, trailing only Harden, Stephen Curry, Damian Lillard and James.

Doncic, whose 62-foot heave at the halftime buzzer keyed Friday's comeback win, joined Bryant, Elgin Baylor and George Mikan as the only Lakers to score at least 40 points in four consecutive games.

"[Doncic] is the MVP right now," Blazers coach Micah Nori said during his pregame comments. "Hands down."

articles.headline: Seahawks' Quenton Nelson, Sam Darnold among starters ruled out
articles.description: New Seahawks trade acquisition Quenton Nelson will have a "minor procedure" and is one of six starters, including QB Sam Darnold, who won't play vs. the Cardinals.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスのクエントン・ネルソンとサム・ダナルドが先発メンバーから外れる
articles.descriptionJa: シーホークスがトレードで獲得したばかりのクエントン・ネルソンが「軽微な処置」を受けることとなり、QBサム・ダナルドを含む6人の先発選手がカーディナルズ戦を欠場する。
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- One week after arriving via a trade, Seattle Seahawks All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson needs a "minor procedure" on his knee, coach Mike Macdonald said Friday.

Sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport that Nelson's surgery will be to clean out cartilage in his knee.

Macdonald said Nelson will not go on injured reserve, and he'll be designated as week-to-week.

Nelson and quarterback Sam Darnold, who has a quad injury, are among six starters ruled out by the Seahawks (4-4) for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals (3-5) at Lumen Field. The others are defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger), outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) and wide receiver/returner Rashid Shaheed (knee).

While Nelson is out, Seattle will move Grey Zabel back to left guard and reinsert Anthony Bradford into the starting lineup at right guard. After acquiring Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, the Seahawks moved Zabel to right guard, where Bradford had been their starter.

"He had something that he was dealing with when he got here and we re-imaged it and it was aggravated to some degree," Macdonald said of Nelson's injury. "We've kind of done the due diligence, and everybody agrees that it's best to take care of it now and play the long game. He'll be week-to-week at this point."

Nelson, 30, played every offensive snap in the Seahawks' loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night. He was seen this week with a sleeve on his right leg, was listed as limited Wednesday and did not practice the past two days.

"I can't give you all the details on what it was and what we found," Macdonald said. "Obviously, he passed the physical, so I think two things are true: One, that it was something that he was dealing with coming out of whatever game it was before the trade, and I think it's been aggravated since he got here."

Darnold, who suffered a cracked rib on the second play of Monday's game and then injured his quad toward the end of the game, will not go on IR, Macdonald said.

Macdonald on Friday said Drew Lock will be the starter against the Cardinals, despite a right elbow injury that had him inactive the past two games and limited his throwing in recent weeks. He was again listed as a limited participant Friday, as he has been on all 12 injury reports released since the start of Week 6.

Macdonald said earlier in the week that the Seahawks had to also get Jalen Milroe, who has not appeared in a regular-season game since Week 5 of last year, ready to play in case they needed to turn to their third quarterback against Arizona. He said Friday that they've had to manage Lock's reps this week, which was "more precautionary than anything else."

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 9 Buzz

Biggest concerns ahead of Sunday

Players with early starts

 Deshaun Watson, QB, Browns (concussion): Watson missed practice to start the week before upgrading to limited Friday. While he is listed as questionable for Week 9, Shedeur Sanders will start in his place. Sanders does add some value with his legs, having rushed for over 20 yards in five of eight games last season. However, he had just one game in which he threw for multiple TDs or more than 210 yards (both coming in the same game). Even in a favorable matchup against the Saints, Sanders is only for those in need in superflex leagues.

 Harold Fannin Jr., TE, Browns (groin): Fannin was added to the injury report Thursday, before being removed Friday. He does not carry an injury designation and will play in Week 9. He is a strong play in fantasy this week. It's a favorable matchup against the Saints for Fannin, who averaged 14.6 fantasy PPG with Sanders last year (9.9 with other QBs) and is coming off two huge performances.

 George Pickens, WR, Cowboys (hamstring): Pickens was limited all week at practice and the Cowboys are hopeful he will play, despite him being listed as questionable for Week 9. Even though he has not duplicated his success from last season, Pickens still needs to be started each week. If TE Jake Ferguson sits, it could mean some added targets his way. If Pickens were to sit, Ryan Flournoy would be a worthy streaming option.

articles.headline: Jacoby Brissett brings hope but realistic expectations for spiraling Ravens
articles.description: The Ravens know what they're getting in acquiring veteran journeyman QB, but does Jacoby Brissett know what he's in for?
articles.headlineJa: ジャコビー・ブリスセット、低迷するレイブンズに希望をもたらすも、期待値は現実的なものに
articles.descriptionJa: レイブンズはベテランのジャーニーマンQBを獲得することで何が得られるかを理解しているが、ジャコビー・ブリスセット自身は自分がどのような状況に身を投じるのかを理解しているだろうか？
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens understand what they're getting in acquiring veteran journeyman quarterback Jacoby Brissett. But does Brissett realize the situation he's coming into with the Ravens?

The Ravens officially finalized their trade with the Arizona Cardinals on Friday by sending a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-rounder in exchange for Brissett and a 2027 fourth-round selection. Baltimore knows it's adding an experienced starting-caliber quarterback who has a track record of completing over 60% of his passes and directing a middle-of-the-road offense.

For Brissett, he's not just coming into a situation where he's trying to keep the Ravens' season afloat in case an injured Lamar Jackson (right thumb) can return by the end of the season. Brissett is taking over an offense that looks broken, from the lack of discipline to poor blocking to the historic struggles to score.

The Ravens (4-5) have failed to score more than 14 points in four straight games, which is a team record in futility. This didn't happen when Baltimore went through a five-game touchdown drought in 2000. This didn't happen when first-round quarterback Kyle Boller turned out to be a bust in 2003. This didn't happen in 2015 when the Ravens started Matt Schaub, Jimmy Clausen and Ryan Mallett after Joe Flacco suffered a season-ending knee injury.

The players aren't blaming the loss of Jackson for the offensive flop, even though the lack of a two-time NFL MVP has certainly pulled the plug on Baltimore's explosiveness. It hasn't helped that top backup Tyler "Snoop" Huntley is out for the season with a turf toe injury.

The arrival of Brissett brings hope but also realistic expectations.

"I think that'll bode well for us," Ravens offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley said after Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. "But there's a lot of things that we need to fix on our end. I don't think anyone can just come in and fix all the problems."

Let's take a look at the problems:

Pre-snap penalties

It really feels like the Ravens' offense leads the league in hurting itself. With four false-start penalties Thursday, Baltimore has now been flagged for false starts 24 times this season, the most in the league.

The Ravens already have more false-start penalties through nine games this season than they did in all 17 games last season (19 false starts). Part of the problem could be the constant changes due to injuries. Baltimore has had three different starting centers and three different starting quarterbacks.

"It's very frustrating, and again, it's just ownership," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "It's ownership of players and coaches [when] it keeps happening, [but] it's a ninth game, so there's no, 'We haven't done this, we haven't done that or whatever. We've got a new guy in there [at quarterback].' He's been here all season [and] been here all training camp. So, the pre-snap penalties are unacceptable."

articles.headline: Gio Reyna scores, exits with apparent injury ahead of USMNT camp
articles.description: Gio Reyna 's participation for the USMNT in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals could be in jeopardy after he exited Strasbourg's loss with an apparent injury.
articles.headlineJa: ジョー・レイナ、ゴールを決めるも負傷の疑いで退場、USMNTキャンプを前に懸念
articles.descriptionJa: ストラスブールの敗戦時に負傷したと思われるジョー・レイナは、コンカカフ・ネーションズリーグ準々決勝におけるUSMNTへの出場が危ぶまれている。
articles.body:
Gio Reyna 's participation for the United States in this month's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals could be in jeopardy after he exited Strasbourg's Ligue 1 loss to Toulouse on Friday with an apparent thigh injury.

Reyna scored his third goal of a bounce back season with Strasbourg in the 67th minute. However, just three minutes later he signaled to the sideline for a substitution after appearing to feel discomfort in his left thigh. After leaving the field, Reyna headed straight down the tunnel.

Earlier this week, the 23-year-old had been named in Mauricio Pochettino's roster to face Haiti in a two-legged quarterfinal series.

The No. 16 United States faces 84th-ranked Haiti on Nov. 14 in Miami and Nov. 17 in Cincinnati for a berth in the Nations League semifinals, which will be played from March 22-30 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

Reyna has suffered a series of injuries in recent seasons that derailed his time in the Bundesliga with Borussia Dortmund and Borussia Monchengladbach and hampered his progress with the U.S. men's national team.

However, following a promising World Cup, Reyna has impressed with his form and fitness this campaign. He started all four games for the U.S. -- all wins -- in the September-October international window, registering two assists.

Reyna wasn't the only American to score in Friday's clash in France's top tier, with defender Mark McKenzie netting Toulouse's second goal in their 3-1 win.

Earlier on Friday, McKenzie was named as a replacement for injured defender George Campbell on the USMNT roster.

Friday's win marked Toulouse's second victory in its last four matches for 10th place. Strasbourg has lost five of its last six matches and sat 13th in the 18-team table.

Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Brandon Aiyuk meets with 49ers, says he's healthy, 'looking to get reinstated'
articles.description: Brandon Aiyuk met with the Niners on Friday to begin hammering out a path toward a divorce that has been more than two years in the making.
articles.headlineJa: ブランドン・アイユク、49ersと面談、「健康状態は良好で、復帰を目指している」と表明
articles.descriptionJa: ブランドン・アイユクは金曜日、2年以上にわたって続いてきた決別への道筋を固めるため、49ersと面談を行った。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Though there are still obstacles to work through, the San Francisco 49ers and wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk finally appear headed toward a resolution to their tumultuous relationship.

Aiyuk, flanked by his agent Drew Rosenhaus, arrived at the Niners' business offices Friday afternoon to meet with the team and begin hammering out a path toward a divorce that has been more than two years in the making.

In his first public comments to Bay Area media since his knee injury in October 2024, Aiyuk offered a brief statement before he and Rosenhaus headed into the meeting, which lasted about an hour and 15 minutes.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk said. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated to the National Football League."

Aiyuk, who tore the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 20, 2024, hasn't played in an NFL game since. After the Niners voided the roughly $27 million in remaining guarantees in his contract in July 2025 because he didn't attend rehab check-ins on the knee, he stopped showing up at the team facility and landed on the reserve/left-team list in December.

Aiyuk did not report for the offseason program or training camp. Because he is on the left-team list, the only way for Aiyuk to play again was to apply for reinstatement with the NFL and report to the 49ers.

Aiyuk recently hired Rosenhaus to represent him, and Aiyuk filed for reinstatement in late October. But he hasn't been reinstated yet, in part because the 49ers have been seeking repayment of about $13 million in bonus money that was previously paid to Aiyuk, a source told ESPN. The league informed Aiyuk this week that he needs to repay that bonus money before reinstatement.

Rosenhaus indicated before Friday afternoon's meeting that the hope was to resolve the necessary issues for Aiyuk to play again.

"Obviously, Brandon is here to meet with the team," Rosenhaus said. "Fortunately, he's feeling good physically. He's healthy. He's ready to get back to work. We don't really have any comment about where he's going to play. We'll keep that between us and the Niners, but obviously, we are here with the right intentions."

If the 49ers and Aiyuk work out an agreement that allows for reinstatement, the team would then have three options. The 49ers could release Aiyuk, a scenario that remains the most likely. They could trade him, a move the 49ers prefer, though they haven't found a trade partner throughout the offseason, and the deadline is Tuesday.

Or the 49ers could add him to the 53-man roster, but that has seemed to be a long shot since general manager John Lynch said in January that Aiyuk played his last snaps for the team.

articles.headline: Giants' Cam Skattebo doubtful vs. Eagles; Malik Nabers 'full go'
articles.description: Giants running back Cam Skattebo is unlikely to play against the Eagles on Sunday, but receiver Malik Nabers is expected to be a "full go" without limitations.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツのカム・スカッテボはイーグルス戦への出場が危ぶまれ、マリク・ネイバースは「完全復帰」
articles.descriptionJa: ジャイアンツのランニングバック、カム・スカッテボは日曜日のイーグルス戦に出場する可能性が低いが、レシーバーのマリク・ネイバースは制限なく「完全な状態」で出場できる見込みだ。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is unlikely to play on the road against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, but wide receiver Malik Nabers is expected to be a "full go" without limitations, coach John Harbaugh said Friday.

Skattebo, who is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game, injured his hamstring in overtime at the Houston Texans on Oct. 25. He didn't practice this week despite having had a bye week to recover.

While it doesn't look good for Sunday, Harbaugh didn't want to close the door completely.

"Yeah, let's keep it open," he said. "Let's keep it open, let's see what happens."

Skattebo leads the Giants with 418 yards rushing on 98 carries. No other player on the team has 100 yards rushing this season.

Nabers, who missed practice Thursday because of his right knee, practiced Friday without an injury designation and is expected to play without any limitations.

"He practiced fully. He was full participation. It's not an issue," Harbaugh said. "He'll be full go for the game."

Nabers has played all seven games for New York this season after suffering a serious knee injury last season. He leads the team with 48 catches for 605 yards and is looking for his fifth straight 100-yard game Sunday against the Eagles.

The Giants (4-2-1) are looking for their first win at Lincoln Financial Field since 2013. Last season, Skattebo suffered a fractured ankle in Philadelphia.

His absence would leave the Giants short-handed at running back. Devin Singletary, who rushed for the game-winning 30-yard touchdown in Houston after being inactive for several games earlier this season, is expected to be the primary back Sunday. Newcomer Greg Desrosiers Jr. and Phil Mafah are other likely options.

Tyrone Tracy Jr. was placed on injured reserve last week with a hamstring injury.

Desrosiers was signed off the Los Angeles Chargers' practice squad to take Tracy's place last week. He's set to play in his first career game. Mafah has appeared in one game and has five career carries, which came for the Dallas Cowboys against the Giants in Week 18 last season.

articles.headline: Frank Lampard unhappy with 3 big referee decisions in Coventry loss to Everton
articles.description: Coventry City manager Frank Lampard was annoyed that a trio of key decisions went against his side in their 3-1 loss to Everton on Friday.
articles.body:
Coventry City manager Frank Lampard was annoyed key decisions went against his side as he felt they should have had two penalties and one of Everton's goals in their 3-1 win on Friday should have been ruled out.

James Tarkowski appeared to pull the hair of Caleb Yirenkyi as the pair challenged for a cross in the first half but no penalty was awarded.

- Anthony Gordon left Premier League for Barcelona to get 'respect' -- he's got it now

- Former England, Wrexham defender Coady retires at 33: 'Lived the dream'

- Coleman back with Rep. Ireland set-up in 'hybrid role'

The same went for Vitaliy Mkykolenko's tackle on Taiwo Awoniyi, which VAR ruled was marginally outside the box, while the second of Thierno Barry's two goals was checked for handball but was allowed to stand.

"For sure, I have looked at them because emotions in the moment, sometimes you can't be clear, but [Tarkowski] pulls on Caleb's hair," said ex-Everton boss Lampard.

"I think that's a hard area to be in. What is a hair pull and what is not? He's decided it is but it's not enough.

"Taiwo, for me, on the line of the box is a penalty. You have to give the foul in real time anyway but the ref let it go. I thought it was a penalty by the time Myko's knee is in the back of Taiwo's knee.

"The Barry [second] one is handball, I've heard it didn't hit his hand but he's flicked it in with the final touch. VAR is there for that. Nothing went for us tonight.

"Well played Everton, they won the game and we knew it would be a tough match, but if three decisions are that big -- I can't sit here and say I know everything and they should give all three of them, but if one or two go our way they would clearly change the game."

Rules were changed in relation to hair pulling this season, with the offence downgraded from a red card in most circumstances, but Lampard still felt the officials got the interpretation wrong.

"I was only told in an interview just now it was a hair pull but not enough of a hair pull," he said. "If they say it's a hair pull, it's a hair pull.

Lampard was seen speaking to fourth official Sam Barrott at the start of the second half.

"The fourth official was staying away from the details," Lampard added. "I didn't get any details on the sideline.

"The rules are fine. It's not a red card and I kind of get that, I think in a game of football a lot of stuff happens and it's not absolutely dramatic, but the rule remains it's foul so I felt it was a foul."

Yann Gboho scored his first goal for Coventry but Barry's double, taking his tally to 10 for the season, was followed by a Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall goal nine minutes from time.

"Fabulous. I just mentioned it then, [Erling] Haaland's worried about him catching him," Everton boss David Moyes, who disagreed with all Lampard's views on the VAR decisions, said of Barry.

"If you look at a lot of the money being paid for big centre-forwards we have paid enough for him, but we took a bit of gamble on him and went early on him."

articles.headline: Nick Bosa back, Christian McCaffrey good to go for Niners
articles.description: The 49ers will have a healthy Nick Bosa for the first time since Week 2, and running back Christian McCaffrey is good to go this week against the Raiders.
articles.headlineJa: ニック・ボサが復帰、クリスチャン・マキャフリーも49ersで出場可能に
articles.descriptionJa: 49ersは第2週以来、初めてニック・ボサが健康な状態で復帰し、ランニングバックのクリスチャン・マキャフリーも今週のレイダース戦に出場できる見込みだ。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers will welcome defensive end Nick Bosa (calf) and running back Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) back from injury on Sunday while receiver Mike Evans will miss his second consecutive game because of Achilles tendinitis.

Bosa, who has been out since before a Week 3 game against Arizona Cardinals, returned to practice this week and participated in some capacity for all three sessions this week. He has no injury designation for Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders and is good to go.

"I feel great," Bosa said. "Bye week was a good extra week for me and I'm ready to go."

Likewise, McCaffrey also does not have an injury designation after suffering a minor hamstring strain in Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons. McCaffrey did not practice on Wednesday, but participated on Thursday and Friday on his way to being cleared.

Much like Bosa, McCaffrey said the Week 8 bye helped his recovery so he would not miss any time.

"It wasn't too bad," McCaffrey said. "I think having the bye week was awesome, but I feel great."

Evans, meanwhile, continues to deal with Achilles tendinitis that flared up in a Week 6 win against the Washington Commanders. He did not play against the Falcons and then had the bye week to continue recovering.

Although Evans has made "a lot of progress," according to coach Kyle Shanahan, the Niners don't want to risk pushing him too hard too soon so his injury doesn't get worse.

"I think you learn from the history," general manager John Lynch told KNBR radio in San Francisco on Thursday. "Christian had this situation and every player is different, every situation is different but you don't want it to become something that really lingers. So, we're trying to knock it out such that when he comes back, we give him the best chance to stay back."

In addition to Evans, the Niners ruled out fellow wideouts Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) for Sunday. Kirk injured his meniscus in practice on Wednesday. It's unclear whether Kirk will need surgery, Shanahan said.

In better receiver news, Shanahan said it's likely the team will activate Demarcus Robinson (ankle) from injured reserve to play against the Raiders. That would leave a group of Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, Brandin Cooks and, likely, KhaDarel Hodge being elevated from the practice squad, as the team's receivers for Sunday.

The 49ers listed Robinson, cornerback Nate Hobbs (adductor), safety Siran Neal (knee, foot) and cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder) as questionable for Sunday. Shanahan said it remains up in the air on whether they'll activate Hobbs from injured reserve this week.

articles.headline: Barry's brace propels Everton up to 5th with win over Coventry
articles.description: Thierno Barry's hot streak fired Everton into the top five as they came from behind to beat Coventry 3-1.
articles.headlineJa: バリーの2ゴールでエヴァートンがコヴェントリーに勝利し5位へ浮上
articles.descriptionJa: ティエルノ・バリーの好調な得点力がエヴァートンを牽引。コヴェントリーに逆転で3-1と勝利し、トップ5入りを果たした。
articles.body:
Thierno Barry's hot streak fired Everton into the top five as they came from behind to beat Coventry 3-1.

Only Manchester City striker Erling Haaland (nine) has more league goals this season after the 24-year-old's double turned things around against former Everton manager Frank Lampard's side.

Barry's rawness can be a source of frustration, as evidenced in the first half when he wasted a good chance to shoot by failing to get the ball out from under his feet, but he came alive inside the six-yard box after the break.

Trailing to Yann Gboho's first goal for Coventry in only his second league appearance, the French forward headed an equaliser before doubling his tally by bundling in a scrappy effort from barely two yards out.

Lampard will argue his side should have had at least one penalty when James Tarkowski appeared to pull the hair of Caleb Yirenkyi with the score goalless in the first half, but their own defending left a lot to be desired.

Barry has now scored in three successive games for first time for Everton and only second time in his career.

He has six in his last seven in all competitions and 10 for the season -- two more than he managed in his maiden campaign.

Somewhat prophetically boss David Moyes, equalling Harry Catterick's record of 592 matches in charge, had said at his pre-match news conference that "Erling Haaland should be worried."

And while, realistically, the Norway international will not be losing any sleep at the thought Barry's form as the club's only recognised striker is proving a major boost.

With Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall chipping in with goals from midfield, scoring the third nine minutes from time, to add to his all-round creativity Moyes is squeezing everything out of his limited resources.

A third successive win also took the focus off the circus surrounding Jack Grealish.

He has been absent for the last four matches after being disciplined by the club for missing training, but he returned to Finch Farm earlier in the day to begin a tailored programme, which is likely to see him return to the first-team fold after the international break.

A nondescript first half which began with Everton in the ascendency finished with the visitors in command and was notable mainly for Tarkowski's tangle with Yirenkyi as they challenged for a cross.

His grasp of the midfielder's hair was so slight it appeared to go unnoticed by everyone except the player and no action was taken by VAR.

Coventry's second penalty appeal was checked by the officials but Vitalii Mykolenko's challenge on Taiwo Awoniyi was ruled to have been made fractionally outside the box.

But when the ball bounced around the area after the visitors were able to play their way from right to left Gboho, surrounded by three Everton players, poked through a shot which appeared to take Pickford by surprise as it crept over the line.

articles.body:
Arsenal and Manchester United are keeping tabs on AFC Bournemouth's Marcus Tavernier, while the Gunners are also now eyeing RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa after Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior turned them down last summer. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal and Manchester United are monitoring AFC Bournemouth midfielder Marcus Tavernier, according to TEAMtalk. The Gunners have been compiling scouting reports on the 27-year-old as they assess options to strengthen their attack, while they also admire his teammate Junior Kroupi. Tavernier, who has scored six goals in 14 appearances this season, is also attracting interest from Newcastle and long-time admirers Tottenham Hotspur.

- RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa is being tracked by Arsenal ahead of the January transfer window, according to The Sun. Nusa, 21, has 16 goals and 18 assists from 85 games at Leipzig and could slot into the left wing slot left open at the Emirates by the exits of Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard, after Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior turned them down last summer. However, Leipzig don't need to raise any funds as they let Yan Diomande move to Real Madrid for €125 million last window, so will look to keep the Norway international even if a bid of €60 million arrives.

- Newcastle United are considering a January move for Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney, as per Football Insider. The 30-year-old has previously worked with Magpies head coach Matthias Jaissle in the Saudi Pro League, which could potentially help get a deal over the line. Manchester United have also shortlisted Toney as they assess options to strengthen their attack following Benjamin Šeško's injury.

- Bayern Munich are considering signing FC Porto winger Oskar Pietuszewski as a backup for Luis Díaz next summer, Sky Germany reports. The 18-year-old has a €60 million release clause in his contract, with Bayern already informed of the details and discussions having taken place. Porto sporting director Max Eberl is a big fan of Pietuszewski, who has been capped six times by Poland since making his international debut at the beginning of the year.

- Arsenal and Manchester City are monitoring Newcastle United full back Tino Livramento, Football Insider has revealed. Both clubs are longstanding admirers of the 23-year-old and have previously seen attempts to sign him blocked by Newcastle. However, the Premier League club could reluctantly sanction his exit next summer if they can't make progress on a new contract, with Livramento's current deal due to expire in 2028.

- Tottenham Hotspur retain first-option matching rights on Harry Kane despite his new Bayern Munich contract running until 2029, according to The Telegraph. articles.headline: Vincent Kompany: Bayern Munich boss close to 'full recovery' after collapse
articles.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany is on track for a "full recovery" after a lengthy absence following his collapse at a training session, assistant Aaron Danks said Friday.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany is on track for a "full recovery" after a lengthy absence following his collapse at a training session, assistant Aaron Danks said Friday.

Kompany has been out of action for two weeks since collapsing at a reserve team training session on Oct. 23. He was hospitalised and treated for meningeal irritation, which is an inflammation of the tissue around the brain or spinal cord.

"I've had a few really good phone calls with Vince," Danks said. "He seems very positive and appears to be well on the way to a full recovery. The international break provides a good opportunity to reflect and see when he can return."

Danks remains in charge for Bayern's game against Mainz on Saturday in the Bundesliga, the team's fifth since Kompany's collapse. After that, an international break means Bayern doesn't play again until Nov. 20.

During Kompany's time away from the club, Harry Kane has became the first Bayern player in 45 years to win the Ballon d'Or and signed a contract extension, while Bayern drew with German rival Borussia Dortmund and beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday, and also suffered a string of injuries.

Bayern set a club policy of not involving Kompany in football discussions during his time recovering at home after he was released from hospital.

- Harry Kane signs new Bayern Munich contract: 'I want to win many more titles'

- Harry Kane falls short of Cristiano Ronaldo Champions League goal streak record

- Teenager Karl propels Bayern Munich to win at Atlético Madrid

Kane said Kompany may not have known in advance when his contract extension was announced Thursday.

"We're really happy that the best player in the world right now has committed to Bayern. He feels really good here. You can also sense that," Christoph Freund, Bayern sporting director, said of Kane's extension. "It's important to have a figure like him here. He's exceeded all expectations from experts.

"We firmly believe he can maintain his level with his attitude and personality and help us. If we didn't believe that, we wouldn't have extended. The truth is on the pitch.

"I believe he'll continue to show that in the coming years."
